items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: I took the job with James Brown... when I got in the James Brown band I found out that I liked it... James Brown did not like it when people tried to take over his band so he fired me

ctx.x: Did spending time at the piano help with the improvising? Because I know, I read in your book that you had the typical sort of classical lessons, but, I actually have a quote here. You wrote: “ I just didn’t want to be this Glen Howard guy who played the hell out of Rachmaninoff. I wanted to play the shit out of the trombone solo in “Things Ain’t What They Used to Be.”

Yeah, yeah. Well you know Gwen Howard was a girl. And I didn’t want to play that nice little dainty music like girls played you know. I wanted to play like “Things Ain’t What It Used to Be.” So that was in my head you know. I can play the boogie woogie on the piano with my left hand and in my right hand I played the chord. I didn’t know what I was doing but I was hearing it in my head you know. So that’s what I learned before I learned music. You know? I knew how to play, how to improvise and how to make up music…

Well you set up one of my questions that I’ve really been curious about so we can jump there. I used to be — I’ve been in a lot of bands and as a horn player for some reason I got the job of writing out the horn parts that we were hearing on records. And it was a laborious process, especially with those funk rhythms and all the sixteenth rests. When you talked about not doing that until you were with James Brown, was it tedious for you to write those parts out or didn’t you even write them out?
